To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exercise induces cerebral vascular endothelial cell growth factor and angiogenesis via a receptor in the brain that recognizes lactate.
exercise induces cerebral VEGFA and angiogenesis via a receptor (lactate receptor HCAR 1) expressed on brain vascular cells.
lactate induces cerebral angiogenesis and VEGF via the lactate HCAR1 receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of physical exercise on brain function, which are of relevance to the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
a new signaling pathway from skeletal muscle to brain that can improve brain function, and delay or even reverse neurodegeneration in aging and in diseases such as Alzheimer's.
the molecular mechanism of exercise-induced brain angiogenesis, which may have important implications for the development of novel therapies for brain diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lactate released from skeletal muscle during exercise induces angiogenesis in the brain by activation of the lactate receptor in the pial fibroblasts lining the cerebral blood vessels.
the HCAR1 is a lactate sensor that mediates the exercise-induced increase of VEGF and cerebral angiogenesis.
HCAR1 activation in the brain is a key mediator of the beneficial effects of physical exercise on brain function and structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCAR1, a lactate receptor, is highly expressed in brain endothelial cells and in perivascular cells.
HCAR1 is a receptor in pial fibrotic cells that mediates lactate-induced VEGFA and angiogenesis, and that HCAR1 mediates exercise-induced angiogenesis in brain.

lactate released by exercising muscle activates HCAR1 on the brain endothelial cells, which in turn leads to the production of VEGFA, a potent inducer of angiogenesis, and that this process is critical for the exercise-induced angiogenesis in brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise induces cerebral VEGFA and angiogenesis via a lactate receptor in brain endothelial cells.
exercise induces angiogenesis in the brain through the lactate receptor, HCAR1.
exercise induces cerebral angiogenesis and that this effect is dependent on the lactate receptor, HCAR1.
